nicknames: Where the Turf Meets the Surf

main_dirt.bias_notes: Main track strongly favors early speed and tactical pressers (over 80% of dirt sprint winners race on or near the lead). Deep closers are at a severe disadvantage in sprints. The coastal marine layer can tighten the surface early in the day, creating extreme speed-bias conditions ('Golden Rail'). Kickback is severe, so horses forced to eat dirt inside often give up.
main_dirt.post_bias: In 1-mile dirt routes, the gate is close to the first turn; inside posts (1-4) hold a significant advantage, while horses in post 7 or wider are forced to use early energy to avoid going wide. In sprints, middle and outside posts are preferred to avoid kickback.

jimmy_durante_turf.bias_notes: A 7/8-mile oval set inside the main track featuring a diagonal chute. Turf Sprints are run strictly at 5 Furlongs (no 5 1/2F sprints). Turf routes play very fair to late closers—front-runners win under 20% of turf routes, while stalkers and deep closers dominate (80%+ win rate).
jimmy_durante_turf.post_bias: In 5F turf sprints, post position is fair, but early speed is key. In 1 1/16M and 1 1/8M turf routes, posts 7 and outward are a major disadvantage due to tight turns; inside posts (1-5) saving ground are heavily favored.

handicapping_angles.the_marine_layer_effect: When the coastal marine layer rolls in and the track retains moisture, the dirt becomes tight and extremely speed-favoring ('Golden Rail'). On dry, hot afternoons, the dirt gets deep and loose, upgrading tactical stalkers.
handicapping_angles.5f_turf_sprint_speed: All turf sprints at Del Mar are 5 Furlongs. Look for horses with proven 21.x first-quarter speed. Stalkers can win, but pure closers run out of stretch length.
handicapping_angles.ship_and_win_invaders: Del Mar's lucrative 'Ship & Win' program offers a $4k-$5k appearance fee + 40-50% purse bonus for out-of-state shippers. Heavily upgrade East Coast and Midwest shippers from top barns (e.g., Maker, Diodoro, Motion).
handicapping_angles.trainer_clues: Bob Baffert is lethal with dirt 2YO first-time starters (MSW), but struggles in Maiden Claiming. Phil D'Amato dominates turf routes with layoff returners (90+ days). Peter Miller excels with big class drops into claiming ranks.
